passages.provision_quote: A public agency shall not impose or enforce any minimum automobile parking requirement on a residential, commercial, or other development project if the project is located within one-half mile of public transit.
passages.note: Statewide preemption removing local minimum-parking mandates near transit; the bill text page names no voter.
Assembly floor concurrence vote; Aguiar-Curry voted Aye. Page prints no provision text.
passages.actor_quote: Ayes Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Bennett, Berman, Bloom

rows.reasoning: AB 2097 eliminates minimum automobile parking requirements near transit statewide, removing the very thing rung 5 names as "the foundation of local transportation policy" ("abundant free parking"). Her Aye vote shows direction away from rung 5, but a single deregulation act cannot establish how she would prioritize investment among rungs 1 through 4, which differ on the balance of pedestrian/transit/cycling investment against road capacity.
needs_source: Her own statement or record tying this vote (or another act) to a specific transportation-investment priority among rungs 1-4, e.g. a floor speech, press release, or questionnaire answer on road vs. transit/bike/pedestrian spending.
